title: Block Copolymer Micelles for Co-Delivery of Pharmacologically Active Substances
content: Self-assembly of block copolymers into polymeric micelles has emerged as a promising strategy for drug delivery, not only in the context of monotherapy, but also as part of combination therapy. Polymeric micelles have, indeed, shown great promise as drug delivery systems due to their stability, biocompatibility and high drug loading. Co-encapsulating pharmacological agents further aims to ameliorate their therapeutic outcome, while improving adverse effect profiles and enhancing patient safety. The present review focuses on summarizing the recent advances in the formulation of co-loaded polymeric micelles. Innovative solutions for the co-encapsulation of drugs with formulation issues, such as low lipophilicity, are briefly discussed. In addition, we examine the impact of size, morphology and structure modulation of the polymeric micelles on the biological behavior and mainly drug release rate. Functionalization is also critically discussed, as it is considered one of the most important features of polymeric micelles. When it comes to the delivery of multiple drugs at once, targeting is deemed especially important for therapeutic efficacy. Furthermore, the formulation of stimuli-responsive micelles has been one of the greatest achievements of the field, as it allows for a more controlled release of the co-encapsulated agents. Finally, examples of advanced and diagnostic treatments concerning co-loaded drugs into polymeric micelles are discussed. This review aims to aid future attempts in achieving synergistic therapeutic effects through polymeric micelles, successfully reaching clinical applicability. Thus, we will revisit the current progress of the existing literature and critically discuss key points, limitations, gaps and prospects of the field.
